title: The adjoint quotient in semisimple rank one is PGL2
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Reductivity and maximal tori have the meanings of [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. The centre $Z(G)$ is the subgroup functor of points commuting with every point after every commutative algebra extension. Quotients are represented fppf sheaf quotients as in [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry]. Let $G$ be reductive and $R(G)$ its largest smooth connected solvable normal subgroup. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Assume that every maximal torus of $G/R(G)$ has dimension one. Then there exists a faithfully flat homomorphism $q:G\to\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$ with scheme-theoretic kernel exactly $Z(G)$; in particular $G/Z(G)\simeq\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$. Here $\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$ is the fppf sheaf quotient of the invertible $2\times2$ matrices by scalar matrices [lem-sfb-projective-matrix-central-cover]. No hypothesis on the characteristic is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 20.22, printed p.415, and Theorem 20.16, pp.412--413: action on the Borel quotient projective line has kernel the full scheme-theoretic centre.

proof.text: Choose a maximal torus $T$ and a Borel $B^+$ containing it using [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety] and [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] (start with the trivial torus). By [lem-sfb-rank-one-opposite-borel-intersection] there is the other Borel $B^-$. Put $C=G/B^+$. The homogeneous quotient exists and its $F$-points are $G(F)/B^+(F)$ by [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. The quotient map is flat, surjective and finitely presented by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient], so [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry] gives smoothness, properness and integrality of $C$. Finally [lem-sfb-rank-one-flag-curve] gives $\dim C=1$.

Left multiplication descends to an action of $G$ on the right-coset fppf sheaf $C$: $g\cdot(hB^+)=(gh)B^+$. This is well defined on cosets, commutes with scalar extension and hence sheafifies. It is transitive on $C(F)$ by the quotient description. It cannot be the trivial action: otherwise its orbit map $G\to C$ at $eB^+$ would be constant, whereas it is the surjective quotient map onto the one-dimensional integral scheme $C$. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-curve-connected-linear-action] to obtain $C\simeq\mathbf P^1_F$. By [lem-sfb-projective-frames-pgl] its automorphism sheaf is $\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$, giving a homomorphism $q:G\to\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$ that realizes this action.

Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to factor $q$ as $G\xrightarrow{u}I\hookrightarrow\operatorname{PGL}_2$, with $u$ faithfully flat. The map $F[I]\to F[G]$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with $N=F[I]$. Since $G$ is smooth its coordinate ring is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied over the field $F$; thus $I$ is reduced. The spectrum map for $u$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Its continuous image is connected since $G$ is connected, so $I$ is connected. If $I$ were proper, [lem-sfb-pgl2-proper-connected-subgroup-solvable] would make $I$ smooth and solvable. Then [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point] applied to its action on the nonempty proper curve $C$ gives a point fixed by $I$ and hence by $G$. This contradicts the transitivity on $C(F)$ and $C\simeq\mathbf P^1_F$, which has the distinct points $0$ and $\infty$. Therefore $I=\operatorname{PGL}_2$ and $q$ is faithfully flat.

Let $K=\ker q$, a closed normal finite-type subgroup scheme (the fibre over the identity of the affine finite-type group). An element of $K(A)$ fixes every $A$-point of $C$, and in particular $eB^+$, whose stabilizer is $B^+$ by the quotient kernel-pair description. Thus $K\subseteq B^+$. Choose $n\in G(F)$ with $nB^+n^{-1}=B^-$ using [lem-sfb-torus-normalizer-borel-transitivity]. Normality gives $K=nKn^{-1}\subseteq B^-$. Consequently [lem-sfb-rank-one-opposite-borel-intersection] gives $K\subseteq T$ scheme-theoretically. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable], $K\simeq\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$. Conjugation by the smooth connected group $G$ acts on $K$ by group automorphisms; [lem-sfb-connected-action-multiplicative-type-rigidity] makes this action trivial. Hence $K\subseteq Z(G)$, on every test algebra and every further extension.

The centre is represented by a closed normal subgroup by [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change]. Every central element centralizes $T$ after every algebra extension; [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] therefore gives $Z(G)\subseteq T\subseteq B^+$. For any $F$-algebra $A$, $z\in Z(G)(A)$ and any $x\in C(A)$, lift $x$ fppf locally to $g\in G(A\prime)$ using [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. There $z\cdot x=zgB^+=gzB^+=gB^+=x$. Since $C$ is the represented fppf sheaf quotient these equalities descend, and persist after every further extension. Thus $z$ acts as the identity automorphism, $q(z)=1$, and $Z(G)\subseteq K$. Combined with the preceding step this gives $K=Z(G)$ as subgroup schemes.

source.place: Theorem 20.22, p.415; scheme-theoretic maximal-torus centralizer, Theorem 17.59, p.371.

proof.text: Let $p:G\to Q=G/Z(G)$ be the quotient of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], so $p$ is faithfully flat with kernel $Z(G)$. By [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal], $q$ factors uniquely as $a\circ p$ and $p$ factors uniquely as $b\circ q$, because their kernels coincide. Uniqueness in that same statement, applied to $p$ and to $q$, gives $ba=\operatorname{id}_Q$ and $ab=\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{PGL}_2}$. Thus $a:Q\simeq\operatorname{PGL}_{2,F}$, and the asserted faithfully flat $q$ has exactly the full scheme-theoretic centre as kernel. No step required division by the characteristic or reducedness of the kernel.

Item statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to live. The item is still unsplit live, there is no repair note, none of the new ids exists live, and no proof_dep reaches back to the item (no cycle). Source checks in Milne iAG2017: Thm 20.22 (p.415), 20.16 (a)-(d) (pp.412-413), 20.18 and 20.21 (B+ ∩ B- = T), 20.5 (p.408; the acting group must be affine, which the node requires), 17.27 (p.360). Steps: (1) Borel, maximal torus T, the opposite Borel, and C = G/B+ smooth, proper, integral of dimension 1. (2) The coset action is nontrivial because its orbit map is the quotient map onto a curve; complete-curve gives C ≅ P1, and projective-frames-pgl gives q (that PGL2 is a scheme and the Zariski quotient, so it equals the fpqc quotient). (3) The flat-image factorisation gives I, which is reduced (inside F[G]) and connected (surjective Spec); if I were proper the new node would make it solvable, the fixed-point node would give a G-fixed point, contradicting transitivity on P1; so q is faithfully flat. (4) ker q lies in B+ (stabiliser via the kernel pair) and in B- (normal, Borels conjugate), hence in T scheme-theoretically; it is diagonalizable, and multiplicative-type rigidity makes it central. (5) Z(G) ⊆ C_G(T) = T ⊆ B+, and zgB+ = gzB+ = gB+ fppf-locally, so Z(G) ⊆ ker q; this avoids needing Z(PGL2) = e. (6) The universal property applied to both quotient maps gives the isomorphism. New nodes are true; small cases checked: SL2 (kernel mu2, including char 2), GL2, PGL2, products with tori; nonsolvable A5 shows the reduced+connected hypothesis is needed; an elliptic curve acting on itself shows affineness is needed. No duplicates: the root-data intersection and dichotomy nodes sit downstream of the item, so citing them would be circular; other candidates checked. No SGA. No changes made.
